results.label: this tree ships the plan gate (src/bots/plan-gate.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the parent tree IS the committed release this milestone is built on: it carries the review periods and the clean-rep count, and no plan gate of its own
the fixture is the SAME shape in both trees: the same four plans, the same stored bytes and the same trades
the delivered tree creates exactly the parent’s schema: every table, index and trigger is byte-identical DDL, so this milestone adds NO schema object of any kind
and on that fixture every table is byte-identical, so nothing was back-filled or rewritten at open time either
there is no plan_gate/plan_rule table, index or trigger to find: the schema search the negative claim rests on is empty in both trees
the four stored shapes really are the four shapes being measured, written by each tree’s own database layer
the parent’s own second boot performs its M102 v1 backfill exactly once (four version rows) and a further boot changes not one byte
and the parent stores every one of the four shapes without an opinion about any of them: an array, a double-encoded string, and prose all sit in the column, read by nobody on the decision path
the parent’s own decision surface has NO plan keys at all — no `plan_rules` on a candidate and no `plan_gate` in the filter block, measured over a real analysis
and the parent ships no plan-gate module — the absence is real, not a configuration of this probe
the delivered tree reads the PARENT’s own plan: two machine lines enforced, one line of prose reported and never interpreted
the prose-only plan enforces nothing and SAYS so (it does not look satisfied), and its free-text market-conditions field is not parsed
a `require` line outside the vocabulary is surfaced as unrecognised with its reason, so a typo is named instead of silently passing
the double-encoded value the parent stored is reported MALFORMED rather than read as a satisfied plan
with no id named the gate uses the parent’s own `active` column: the one active plan, and only because it is the only one
the version it reports is the parent’s own M102 row for that plan, so a refusal can name the rule set the trade was taken under
reading the plan writes NOTHING: every table digest is identical before and after, and the versions table did not move
and reading it a second way is stable: the same four rows produce the same verdicts as the parent’s file is re-opened and read again
the vocabulary and the limits travel with the module itself — thirteen concrete lines and the read-only claim the refusal can be quoted against
the parent’s own code still opens the file afterwards and sees exactly the four plans and two trades it left, with no row and no column this milestone added

scope: M56 migration: a plan the committed parent stored is read with no schema change and no write: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
